beats.care: India has a similar power, President's Rule under Article 356. This is a live example of a central government taking over an opposition-run state.
beats.what: Pakistan's president declared an emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Sunday. The governor now runs the province, and the army has been deployed.
beats.why: The government cites terrorism and law and order. Imran Khan's party PTI, which runs the province, calls it undemocratic and will fight it in court.

cards.body: PTI says Chief Minister Sohail Afridi and other leaders were detained. Governor Faisal Karim Kundi, from a party allied with the government, now runs the province with an 11-member advisory council. Schools in Peshawar and nearby cities were shut on Monday.

a.body: Militant violence has reached an unprecedented level, and the provincial government was indifferent in the fight against terrorism.
a.label: Government says

b.body: It's an undemocratic move against an elected government. Security problems are in some districts, so why take over the whole province?
b.label: PTI says

cards.note: Officials have not made public evidence for their claim that the provincial government has militant links.
cards.title: Was the emergency needed?

cards.body: Already more than all of 2025 (1,066), according to the think tank PICSS.
cards.caption: Militant attacks in Pakistan, Jan–Sep 2026

cards.body: Pakistan's provinces have been put under governor's rule at least eight times since 1949. This province also faced it in 1975 and 1994.

cards.q: Can a central government ever justify taking over a state?

opts: The federal government runs it, not elected leaders
cards.q: What does emergency rule change in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
cards.why: Under emergency rule, Islamabad takes control and the elected provincial government is sidelined.

cards.outcome: Yes. Both houses of Parliament endorsed the emergency on 14 Oct, a week before the deadline, as opposition members protested and walked out.
cards.q: Will Pakistan's Parliament approve the emergency by 21 Oct?

cover.label: Emergency clause used on Khyber Pakhtunkhwa

hook: Why did Pakistan just *take over* a whole province?

learn.t: Pakistan's constitution lets the president declare an emergency over 'internal disturbance', so the federal government can run a province directly.

tldr: Pakistan has put Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the province run by jailed ex-PM Imran Khan's party, under emergency rule, citing terrorism and law and order.
watch: Both houses of Pakistan's Parliament must approve the emergency by 21 October. Watch whether it passes.
